text:
sara: Hey team — customer acct-7890 says their paid balance was consumed before promo credits. Dashboard shows 720 promo credits remaining but invoice charged for 18k tokens. Customer says this happened after a promo top-up last week.

mike: Account ID and approximate time range? I'll pull the ledger.

sara: acct-7890, happened between 2026-02-14 03:40 UTC and 2026-02-14 04:15 UTC. They attached a screenshot of the dashboard (claims 720 promo credits left) and a download of the invoice that charged $9.12 for usage.

thomas: Can you paste a sample request id from the customer's API request headers (x-request-id) or a message id from their app logs? Need something to correlate.

sara: They sent request-id `req_9c3f2a`. Also they ran a bulk embedding job: curl -i -H "Authorization: Bearer <key>" -d '{"input": ["...lots..."]}' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings

emily: Pulling billing ledger for acct-7890 now.

billing-bot: Running query: SELECT applied_at, source_type, source_id, tokens_applied, remaining FROM credit_ledger WHERE account_id='acct-7890' ORDER BY applied_at ASC;

billing-bot: Result (trimmed):
2026-02-10T12:05Z | promo | promo_2026feb_topup | 5000 | remaining: 720
2026-02-12T09:01Z | paid_balance | charge_2026-02-12 | 25000 | remaining: 0
2026-02-14T03:44Z | usage | req_9c3f2a | tokens: 18000 | applied_to: charge_2026-02-12

thomas: Hmm — ledger shows usage applied to paid_balance (charge_2026-02-12) instead of promo_2026feb_topup. That suggests burn-order logic selected paid_balance first for that window.

mike: Any recent deploys touching burn order or expiry logic? We rolled out RB-9465 last week around midnight on 2026-02-13 which changed concurrency behavior of the credit applier.

thomas: I can reproduce locally if the expiry sweep job and the usage-applier run concurrently. Repro steps:
1) Create account with promo credit (promo_1 with expiry 2026-02-15T00:00Z) and a paid balance.
2) Kick off a large usage job that races with the expiry_sweep. Usage applier acquires no account lock -> it reads ordered buckets but before it writes, expiry job marks promo bucket as expired.
3) Usage applier writes consumption against next available bucket (paid_balance).

thomas: Local reproduction log snippet:
```
[03:43:10] expiry_sweep: marking promo_1 expired
[03:43:11] usage_applier: read buckets -> promo_1 (status: active)
[03:43:11] usage_applier: applying tokens -> writes to paid_balance
[03:43:11] expiry_sweep: finalized promo_1 expired
```

emily: So race causes promo to look available to the reader but be expired by writer commit ordering. Dashboard cache then shows old remaining (720) because cache TTL is 5m and backing read replaced later.

mike: Impact: some customers may get charged paid balance when promo should have been used; invoices reflect that and dashboard can be inconsistent briefly. Root cause = missing account-level locking around burn/expiry updates after RB-9465 concurrency change.

sara: Customer is asking for immediate remediation and adjustment to invoice. Can we credit them back for the misapplied tokens?

thomas: We'll need to correct the ledger: reassign the 18k tokens from charge_2026-02-12 to promo_2026feb_topup and mark charge_2026-02-12 restored. Then issue a credit memo for $9.12. I'll create a patch and ETA ~2 hours for safe rollback+reassign script.

mike: I'll authorize a customer credit now so they aren't blocked. Issued temporary account credit: credit_tx_8921, amount: $9.12. Sara please tell customer we've applied a temporary credit and we're fixing the ledger permanently.

sara: Noted. I'll update customer: "We've applied a temporary credit of $9.12 and are running a fix to reassign charges. Expect a ledger correction and a final credit memo within 2-3 hours. Sorry about the disruption." :applause:

thomas: Patch implemented: RB-9982. Locking added to credit applier, expiry sweep now takes account-level mutex for same time window. Running reassign script against acct-7890 now.

billing-bot: Reassign script output: moved 18000 tokens from charge_2026-02-12 -> promo_2026feb_topup; updated remaining promo -> 0; restored paid_balance -> 18000 tokens returned.

thomas: Pushed ledger correction and created credit memo CM-2026-211 for $9.12. Also added backfill job to find other accounts hitting the race (query: detect usage_applier applied_to paid_balance while promo existed within last 24h). Backfill candidate list = 7 accounts.

mike: Created follow-up ops ticket RB-10110 to contact affected customers and issue credits for the 7 accounts. Also scheduled a major test to run concurrency stress tests before next deploy.

sara: Customer update: "Thanks — temporary credit visible. We'll wait for final memo. Appreciate the quick turnaround." :thumbsup:

emily: Postmortem note: short-term mitigation = increase expiry_sweep ordering guard and reduce cache TTL to 30s for balances. Long-term = account-level ledger locks + extra unit tests.

sara: Closing thread once RB-9982 & RB-10110 done. Thanks all. :sparkles:
